CART DUST ON THE GROUND: a low warm dust hanging over the trodden ground where the carts have passed, softening the wall's far end into a pale gentle haze
CHIMNEY PLUME STANDING: a fat plume of chimney smoke standing straight up past the rooftops, spreading slow and wide as it climbs into the still air above
COOKING SMOKE ALONG THE FOOT: a low blue haze of cooking smoke lying along the wall's foot, pooling in the quiet places and thinning where the ground opens
DUST MOTES IN THE LIT PLACES: dust motes turning slowly in the lit places between the gate posts, each one catching the warm air and drifting a little before settling
SMOKE LEANING ONE WAY: thin smoke leaning all one way over the rooftops, the whole drift going steady and soft across the upper air above the gate
WARM ARRIVAL HAZE: a warm haze hanging over the whole approach and softening the town above the wall into flat pale bands that sit one behind the other
LAMP BLOOM IN SOFT AIR: the air soft and warm so every lamp along the wall wears a gentle bloom, the glow sitting full and round in the thickened air
GOLDEN DEPTH HAZE: a faint golden haze thickening the depth into flat steps, each band of distance a little softer and a little warmer than the one before
FAR END GOING PALE: the far end of the wall going soft and pale while the near air stays open, the distance dissolving gently into a warm bright flatness
DUSTY GOLD AIR: a dusty gold air with the light sitting in it, the whole space between the traveller and the gate feeling full and faintly luminous
ROSY AIR BETWEEN THE LAMPS: the air gone rosy and soft between the lamps, the warmth of each bloom spreading out until the whole passage glows with it
WASHED BRIGHT AND CLEAR: the air washed clean and bright so every far roof tile and window slit is crisp and hard-edged, the whole depth reading sharp and true
SHARP CLARITY ALONG THE WALL: a sharp clarity all the way along the wall, each stone course and iron fitting sitting clear and precise in the open air
COLOURS AT FULL: clean air with every colour at its most saturated, the painted timbers and dressed stone holding their hues all the way into the depth
FRESH READABLE BRIGHTNESS: a fresh brightness with every pixel edge readable, the lines of mortar and the shapes of the brackets staying crisp from near to far
COLD CLEAN LITTLE SHADOWS: cold clean air and hard little shadows lying flat under every sill and overhang, the whole face of the gate sharp against the sky
FINE RAIN ON THE COBBLES: a light warm rain stippling the cobbles in fine pixel dots, the colours going deeper and richer wherever the wet has settled
LAST OF THE SHOWER: the last of a shower easing off and the puddles still ringed all over, each ring spreading slow and round before it fades into the flat water
FAT SLOW DROPS LANDING: fat slow drops landing one at a time on the stone, each making one bright ring that opens wide and then flattens away into the wet
WATER OFF THE LEDGES: water running off the ledges in bright threads, each thread catching the air for a moment before it joins the wet on the ground below
WET AIR WITH ONE BRIGHT BREAK: the air still wet and everything saturated, one bright break opening in the grey and the colours deepening wherever it reaches
FAT SLOW SNOWFLAKES: fat slow snowflakes coming down in flat pixel dots and settling on every ledge and in the joints of the stone with a soft patient weight
LOW WHITE MIST ON THE GROUND: a low white mist lying on the ground and hiding the wall's foot, the stone rising clean out of it while the mist stays still below
SOFT VEIL LIFTING OFF THE WATER: a soft veil lifting off the wet ground and fading before it reaches the parapet, the air between thinning gently as it rises
DRY SNOW IN THE JOINTS: fine dry snow lying in the joints of the stone and along every ledge, the pale lines picking out every course and cap across the whole face
